extracted.intended_audience: artists, critics, philosophers, and general readers interested in aesthetics and evaluating art
extracted.subtask_description: Developing a definition of art and principles for judging art's value, emphasizing transmission of feeling, relation to life and morality, and rejecting pleasure/beauty as the primary criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of beauty/pleasure as art's aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty, or that which pleases us, can in no sense serve as the basis for the definition of art; to see the aim and purpose of art in the pleasure we get from it is to confuse the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defining art by the enjoyment it affords renders definition impossible, since discussions of taste (why one person likes pears and another meat) do not illuminate what is essential in the activity; basing aesthetics on pleasure simply justifies existing art rather than defines true art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid defining art by its derivation (physiological/evolutionary accounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions that derive art from sexual desire, play, or pleasurable nervous excitation (Schiller, Darwin, Spencer, Grant Allen) are inexact because they treat the origin of art rather than the artistic activity itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such physiological/evolutionary definitions risk including many other human activities (preparing handsome clothes, scents, victuals) and therefore fail to delimit art properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid equating art with mere expression of emotion (experimental definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Making art consist in the external manifestation, by lines, colours, movements, sounds, or words, of emotions felt by man is inexact, because one may express emotions without acting on others; mere expression without infecting others is not art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The capacity to provoke in others the same feeling is essential; private, uncommunicative expression does not satisfy the criterion of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject definitions based on production of pleasure for producer and spectators (Sully critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defining art as production of objects or actions fitted to supply active enjoyment to producer and pleasurable impressions to spectators (apart from personal advantage) is inexact, as it would include conjuring tricks, gymnastic exercises, and exclude works that produce unpleasant but genuine artistic emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art cannot be confined to activities that give pleasure; many true works of art evoke painful or unpleasant sensations yet remain definitively art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as transmission of feeling (core positive definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is a human activity consisting in this, that one man consciously, by means of certain external signs, hands on to others feelings he has lived through, and that other people are infected by these feelings and also experience them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a narrator who evokes his fear of a wolf so hearers feel fear; a painter expressing sorrow so viewers feel it; a composer transmitting delight or despair through sound. The capacity to infect others with the felt emotion is the essential test of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that the artist evoke the feeling in themselves first
rubrics_metrics.description: To evoke in oneself a feeling one has once experienced, and having evoked it in oneself then, by means of movements, lines, colours, sounds, or forms expressed in words, so to transmit that feeling that others may experience the same feeling—this is the activity of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art involves deliberate self-evocation and then mediated transmission; spontaneous contagion (yawning, immediate imitation) is not art because it lacks the intermediate act of deliberate re-evocation and sign-based transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish art from direct contagion
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct, immediate infection (a person making others yawn, laugh, or cry by being in the same present state) does not amount to art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art requires conscious use of external signs to induce feelings in others rather than mere immediate, unmediated imitation or reflexive contagion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate art by its purpose, causes, and effects in human life
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to define and judge art correctly, one must examine the activity in itself, in its dependence on its causes, and in connection with its effects, not merely in relation to the pleasure we can get from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to food: the merit of food is not its taste but its nutritional function; similarly art should be judged by the ends it serves in life and how it influences people and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of art depends on alignment with society's religious/moral sense
rubrics_metrics.description: The estimation of the value of art (i.e. of the feelings it transmits) depends on men’s perception of the meaning of life, defined by what are termed religions; if feelings bring men nearer the ideal their religion indicates they are good, otherwise bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples: medieval Christian societies judged art by whether it evoked piety and renunciation; Greeks judged art by whether it promoted earthly happiness, beauty, and strength; Roman/Chinese standards reflected national/ancestor worship ideals. Thus critics should assess whether transmitted feelings harmonise with the society's moral/religious conception of the good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of post-hoc canons and justificatory definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A common error is to accept a class of works that please a certain circle as 'art' and then devise a definition to include them; aesthetic standards that merely justify existing, canonized works are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not define art by reference to an accepted canon; instead derive a definition from the nature, causes, and effects of the activity itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the broad scope of artistic activity beyond formal arts
rubrics_metrics.description: All human life is filled with works of art of every kind—from cradle-song, jest, mimicry, the ornamentation of houses, dress and utensils, up to church services, buildings, monuments, and triumphal processions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing art, consider informal and everyday forms of transmitted feeling as part of the artistic field; the limited set of 'fine arts' is only a historically selected portion given special importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficacy (infection) is the formal test of art regardless of moral valence
rubrics_metrics.description: The feelings with which the artist infects others may be most various—very strong or very weak, very important or very insignificant, very bad or very good; if only the spectators or auditors are infected by the feelings which the author has felt, it is art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For defining whether something is art, the primary criterion is its ability to transmit the intended feeling; moral assessment (good/bad art) is a separate judgment that depends on broader standards (e.g., religion or conception of the good).

rubrics_metrics.name: Art is indispensable for human union and social life
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is a means of union among men, joining them together in the same feelings, and indispensable for the life and progress towards well-being of individuals and of humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of art should take into account its social function—how it enables sharing of feelings across time and space (access to feelings of contemporaries and those long dead)—and its role comparable to speech in human development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject mystical, metaphysical, or purely physiological accounts as sufficient definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is not the manifestation of some mysterious Idea of beauty or God; it is not merely a play of stored-up energy nor simply the production of pleasing objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid definitions that locate art in metaphysical ideals, in abstract aesthetic essences, or in mere physiological reactions; instead base definition on communicative, functional, and social criteria.
